applyRules: If revision is not the applied revision plus 1, do not apply: drop it when it is not newer, otherwise take view.timeline.snapshot and replace the window.
Remove the rows whose keys are in remove.
Replace each row in upsert in place, found by its key.
Put prepend before the first row and append after the last row, both already in timeline order.
When reorder is present, order the rows by the keys it lists (it lists every row).
Take hasOlder, hasNewer and attachedToLatest, and conversation when present; kind snapshot replaces the whole window.

cases.name: an edited row is replaced in place
a deleted row is removed by key
the ack updates the pending row under the same key
a live message lands before the pending row
the ack moves the row before a later one with a reorder
a skipped revision asks for the snapshot
an update the host already has is dropped
a row filled in between comes with a reorder
rows read towards the latest are appended
going back to the latest is a snapshot
a profile change upserts the rows its person sent

description: Timeline view update vectors (view.updated). Each case is the host's window before an update, one update exactly as the core published it, and the result: applied (with the window after), snapshotRequired (the revision skipped one: the host leaves its window as it is and calls view.timeline.snapshot) or stale (the host already has that revision: the update is dropped). before and after list the rows in timeline order with the three state fields and the revision; the conversation header is not part of them: a host replaces its header whenever an update carries one. core-sdk produces every case in src/client/api/view_window_tests.rs and checks this file against what it produces.
rowKey: clientMsgId when non-empty, else serverId when non-empty, else seq:<conversationId>:<conversationSeq>
